en.title: Payment Intent State Machine with Time-Limited Refunds
en.description:
Execute the interrelated Payment Intent commands from Parts 1–4 of the original Stripe problem. An Intent's states are REQUIRES_ACTION, PROCESSING, and COMPLETED; illegal state transitions and invalid creations/updates are ignored. Command timestamps are strictly increasing. A refund can succeed only for a completed Intent that has not been refunded yet, and it is judged against the merchant's refund time limit.

The input format, examples, and test data were compiled and written by CSWork.
en.input: The first line contains q (1..200000), followed by q lines of commands: `timestamp INIT merchant starting_balance [refund_limit]`, `timestamp CREATE intent merchant amount`, `timestamp ATTEMPT intent`, `timestamp SUCCEED intent`, `timestamp FAIL intent`, `timestamp UPDATE intent new_amount`, or `timestamp REFUND intent`. An ID is a string without whitespace. Balances, amounts, and refund limits are signed 64-bit integers. Only a merchant's first INIT takes effect; duplicate merchants, duplicate Intent IDs, unknown merchants, and negative creation amounts are ignored. A missing or negative refund limit means no time limit, 0 means refunds are not allowed, and a positive n means the refund timestamp must be no later than the success timestamp+n.
en.output: First output the number of initialized merchants; then output `merchant_id balance` line by line in lexicographic order of merchant ID.
en.explanation: Process the input according to the rules above; see the accompanying solution for the approach, correctness proof, and complexity.
hints: Use hash maps to store each merchant's balance/refund limit and each Intent's merchant, amount, state, refund flag, and success time. Scan the commands in time order and update only when the current state satisfies the transition condition; finally, sort the merchants and output them.
